record.paper_title: A Few Problems on Monodromy and Discriminants
record.context_brief: linear-Morse complexity version of greedy simplification
record.original_question: For smooth algebraic hypersurfaces in P(d;N), replace the purely topological complexity measure by the minimal number of critical points of Morse functions obtained as restrictions of linear functions R^N->R to the hypersurface, and allow both topological surgeries and bifurcations of the dual variety that affect this measure. Does the greedy-simplification question remain true in this setting: can every hypersurface be simplified to a trivial one along a generic path whose relevant surgeries and bifurcations always decrease this linear-Morse complexity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{P}(d;N)$ denote the space of real polynomials of degree $\le d$ in $N$ variables, and consider the open subset whose elements define smooth real algebraic hypersurfaces $V_f = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^N : f(x) = 0\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$ (or its projective compactification). For a smooth hypersurface $V \subset \mathbb{R}^N$, define the linear–Morse complexity
$$\mu_{\mathrm{lin}}(V) := \min_{\ell} \#\{\text{critical points of } \ell|_V\},$$
where the minimum is taken over all linear functions $\ell : \mathbb{R}^N \to \mathbb{R}$ whose restriction $\ell|_V$ is a Morse function. Along a generic one-parameter family $\{V_t\}_{t \in [0,1]}$ of hypersurfaces, the value of $\mu_{\mathrm{lin}}$ may change either by a topological surgery of $V_t$ (a Morse modification of the hypersurface) or by a bifurcation of the projective dual variety of $V_t$ (a degeneration of the family of linear restrictions, e.g. a tangency or a coincidence of critical values).

Call a generic path $\{V_t\}_{t \in [0,1]}$ from a hypersurface $V_0$ to a "trivial" hypersurface $V_1$ (e.g. an empty set, a sphere, or a hyperplane) a greedy simplification if at every parameter value $t^* \in [0,1]$ at which a topological surgery or a bifurcation of the dual variety occurs and affects $\mu_{\mathrm{lin}}$, the complexity strictly decreases:
$$\mu_{\mathrm{lin}}(V_{t^*+\varepsilon}) < \mu_{\mathrm{lin}}(V_{t^*-\varepsilon}) \quad \text{for small } \varepsilon > 0.$$

Question: Is it true that every smooth hypersurface $V_0$ defined by an element of $\mathcal{P}(d;N)$ can be connected to a trivial hypersurface by such a greedy-simplification path, i.e., one along which every relevant topological surgery and every relevant bifurcation of the dual variety strictly decreases the linear-Morse complexity $\mu_{\mathrm{lin}}$?

No subsequent paper resolving this specific variant could be located in available search results, so it appears to remain open.
